findings.explanation: Splunkbase 4022 is 'Technical Addon for the Metricator application for Nmon (HEC)', 4856 is 'Metrics Add-on for Infrastructure' (TA-linux-metrics), and 1810 is 'Hunk App for MongoDB'. None is a Cisco ACI, NSX or VMware add-on. The Splunk Add-on for VMware is Splunkbase 3215, and the Cisco ACI add-on in the cached catalogue is 1897, which is deprecated.
findings.quote: **Splunk Add-on for Cisco ACI** ([Splunkbase **4022**](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/4022)); **Splunk Add-on for VMware NSX** ([Splunkbase **4856**](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/4856)); **Splunk Add-on for VMware** ([Splunkbase **1810**](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1810))
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the three IDs. NDFC POAP monitoring needs no ACI, NSX or vSphere add-on, so drop them or keep only 1546 and 7777. If VMware maintenance context really is wanted, cite Splunk Add-on for VMware (Splunkbase 3215).

findings.explanation: The documented NDFC 12 POAP endpoint is GET /appcenter/cisco/ndfc/api/v1/lan-fabric/rest/control/fabrics/{fabricName}/inventory/poap, and discovery is a POST to .../inventory/discover. Neither path cited in the UC appears in the NDFC API reference. The same two paths are repeated in detailedImplementation and implementation.
findings.suggested_fix: Check both paths against the NDFC 12.x API reference. Replace them with the documented POAP inventory endpoint (…/control/fabrics/{fabricName}/inventory/poap) and the documented switch-inventory and event endpoints actually used.

findings.explanation: The NDFC POAP inventory payload exposes serialNumber, model, version, hostname, ipAddress, publicKey, fingerprint and imagePolicy. It does not expose poap_status, bootstrap_phase or error_message. The UC presents these as vendor fields, but they appear to be invented, and the detection depends on them.
findings.suggested_fix: State which NDFC payload or event, if any, carries the POAP phase, status and error text. Otherwise say plainly that these fields come from a site-built normalisation, and describe where failures actually surface (NDFC event and alarm stream, switch syslog during POAP).

findings.explanation: The category guide lists NDFC data only as `cisco:ndfc:event`, in index `cisco_nexus`. None of these five sourcetypes is in the guide, and no add-on produces them. A reader would look for sourcetypes that do not exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Say these are site-defined sourcetypes created on the REST API Modular Input / syslog inputs, or align with the guide's `cisco:ndfc:event` / `cisco_nexus` convention.

findings.explanation: savedsearches.conf has no 'medium' priority. The setting is schedule_priority, with values default, higher or highest.
findings.quote: Schedule the saved search every **5–15m** at **priority=medium**

findings.explanation: The NX-OS default remote-logging facility is local7, and sibling UC-18.4.5 and UC-18.4.6 both say local7.
findings.quote: Forward NDFC and NX-OS syslog streams (often **local6**)
findings.suggested_fix: Say local7 (the NX-OS default), or tell the reader to check the facility set on the `logging server` command.

findings.explanation: implementation and detailedImplementation name `poap_suppress.csv` (serial_number, suppress_until, reason), while knownFalsePositives names a different suppression lookup with different keys. The SPL uses neither.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one suppression lookup, name its keys once, and show the lookup/where clause that applies it.

findings.explanation: detailedImplementation pages at evidence_score ≥ 6 with a freshness gate. The description presents the age_sec breakpoints and evidence_score >= 1 as the alert condition. In the SPL, age_sec only sets the freshness label and never filters.
findings.quote: trigger pages when **evidence_score≥6** and **freshness** is **last_15m** or **last_hour**
findings.suggested_fix: State one alert rule in the description and the alert design: rows are returned at evidence_score ≥ 1, paging happens at ≥ 6 with freshness last_15m/last_hour, and age_sec is a label, not a filter.

findings.explanation: The rex is case-insensitive and matches any alphanumeric token of 11 or more characters, so it is not tight. It also runs on every event; coalesce only prefers structured keys when they are present.
findings.quote: uses a tight **rex** backfill only when structured keys were stripped
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the rex as a loose fallback and give the real NX-OS serial format (for example 3 letters + 8 alphanumerics) the reader should constrain it to.

findings.explanation: The reviewer is an automated agent ('agent-handcraft-2026-04-29'), and the UC carries unverifiable endpoints, fields and wrong Splunkbase IDs. There is no evidence of SME sign-off.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft or community until an SME has checked the NDFC endpoints and payload fields against a live controller.

findings.explanation: NDFC POAP applies to NX-OS-mode Nexus switches. ACI-mode switches are discovered by APIC, not bootstrapped by NDFC POAP. The 'nsx' and 'vmware' equipment tags are unrelated as well.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep cisco_nexus and drop cisco_aci, nsx and vmware.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The serial backfill `rex field=_raw max_match=0 "(?i)(?<![A-Z0-9])(?P<rex_sn>[A-Z0-9]{11}[A-Z0-9]{0,10})"` is case-insensitive with no trailing boundary. Ordinary words of 11+ letters in syslog and audit text ('unreachable', 'provisioning', 'bootstrapping') become rex_sn, and upper() then makes them pass the `^[A-Z0-9]{6,}$` guard. max_match=0 also makes rex_sn multivalue, so sn_norm can be a multivalue field. Failures can be grouped under fake serials. Drop (?i), add a trailing boundary, and match the real Cisco serial pattern.

summary: The POAP/ZTP failure idea is sound and the step-by-step guidance has some real operational content, but the app list cites three Splunkbase IDs that point to unrelated apps. The REST endpoint and the POAP status fields look invented, and the serial-number regex in the SPL will capture ordinary words as serials.
